name: Quan Thang Old House
kicker: Old house open to two streets
summary: A one-storey merchant house more than 150 years old that runs through from Trần Phú to Nguyễn Thái Học. Kim Bồng carpenters cut its woodwork, and the court behind is lined with Chinese ceramics around a sky well and a rockery. Step inside for that court rather than only photographing the tiled front.
fee: 20,000 VND from 10 Aug 2026, or a combination ticket
getThere: Trần Phú or Nguyễn Thái Học; ask for Quân Thắng
heroCaption: The tiled front of Quan Thang house, lanterns by the door

notice.title: Ask for Quân Thắng on the street
notice.body: No street number is published. The house opens onto both Trần Phú and Nguyễn Thái Học, so walk either street and ask for nhà cổ Quân Thắng.

body: Quân Thắng is one of the old houses that still shows how a merchant family lived: more than 150 years old, in the style of the Chinese coast, with woodwork by Kim Bồng carpenters. The one-storey plan runs through from Trần Phú to Nguyễn Thái Học, so you enter on one street and the back is the other.

Inside are the Hội An details: a kẻ chuyền roof frame, a small covered space looking onto a sky well with a chồng rường truss, a crab-shell roof opposite the well, and walls of Chinese ceramics around that court, with a rockery. That court is the reason to go in.
Old houses are optional stops on the old-town ticket. Ask at the booth which ticket covers this one.

admissionNote: No separate price for this building. From 10 Aug 2026: 20,000 VND per person per building, the same for every visitor (Da Nang Resolution 98/2026). Heritage centre notices of 26 Jan and 16 Mar 2026: 80,000 VND (streetscape, Chùa Cầu or Miếu Quan Công, and two other works) or 120,000 VND (adds a museum and three other works), usable through a stay of up to three days. A May 2026 article counts those as four and six works. Ask at the booth which ticket is on sale.
